sentences.text:
8. In Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra [(2011) 1 SCC 694] the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as follows:
111. No inflexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for grant or refusal of anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra [(2011) 1 SCC 694]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: We are clearly of the view that no attempt should be made to provide rigid and inflexible guidelines in this respect because all circumstances and situations of future cannot be clearly visualised for the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: In consonance with the legislative intention the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail should necessarily depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: As aptly observed in the Constitution Bench decision in Sibbia case [(1980) 2 SCC 565 : 1980 SCC (Cri) 465] that the High Court or the Court of Session has to exercise their jurisdiction under Section 438 CrPC by a wise and careful use of their discretion which by their long training and experience they are ideally suited to do.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: In any event, this is the legislative mandate which we are bound to respect and honour.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
10. After bestowing my anxious consideration to B.A.Nos.432 & 440/2024 the facts, the materials placed on record, the rival submission made across the Bar, and on comprehending the nature,
gravity, and seriousness of the offence alleged against the petitioners, that the investigation in the case is only at its nascent stage, that the custodial interrogation of the petitioners is necessary and the recovery is to be effected, I am of the definite view that the petitioners have not made out any exceptional circumstances entitling them to invoke the extra-ordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Section 438 of the Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Therefore, I hold that these are not fit cases to grant orders of pre-arrest bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Consequently, the bail applications are dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 10. Nonetheless, I direct that, if the petitioners surrender before the Investigating Officer within 10 days from today, they shall be interrogated and, thereafter, be produced before the jurisdictional Court on the date of surrender itself.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Then, if the petitioners B.A.Nos.432 & 440/2024 move an application for bail, the jurisdictional Court shall, untrammelled by any observations in this order,
consider the bail application on its merits and as expeditiously as possible.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanju.C.S vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: If the petitioners do not surrender before the Investigating Officer as directed above, the Investigating Officer shall be free to arrest the petitioners as if no order has been passed in this case.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
3. The prosecution case is that the accused shared a common intention and dishonestly induced the de facto complainant to part with money by promising to arrange a job for her son in Indian Railway and also forged an appointment order and showing the same dishonestly obtained Rs.5,00,000/-.
The petitioners filed bail applications before this Court earlier under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
The same was dismissed by this Court as per Annexure-A2 order with a direction to surrender before the investigating officer.
The petitioners are in custody from 23-02-2024 onwards.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are in custody from 23.02.2024 onwards and the petitioners are ready to abide any stringent condition, if this Court grant them bail.
The learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submitted that very serious allegations are there against the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
The allegations against the petitioners are very serious.
But it is a fact that the victims in these cases are giving money to strangers to obtain job in Railways and other Public undertakings when the recruitment in these is done by certain procedures.
Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
The petitioners can be released on bail on condition that if they commit similar offences in future, the investigating officer can file appropriate application before the jurisdictional court and the jurisdictional court can cancel the bail in such situation, even though this bail order is passed by this Court.
6.
Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
i.
Petitioners shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
ii. The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.
The petitioners shall co-operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
iii. Petitioners shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.
iv. Petitioners shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which they are accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
v. The petitioners shall appear before the investigating officer on all Mondays till final report is filed.
vi. 
If any of the above conditions are violated by the petitioners, the jurisdictional Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though the bail is granted by this Court.
